articles.title: Style Observer: A Library to Observe CSS Property Changes
articles.description: Lea Verou is a developer who’s easy to admire because whenever she sets out to solve a problem, the results are always fully formed with no cut corners. So it goes with this ‘exhaustively tested’ JS library for observing changes to CSS properties which deftly handles lots of browser quirks. See the project homepage for more. (TIL there’s a .style TLD!)
articles.author: Lea Verou

articles.title: Why to Move On to 'ESM-Only'
articles.description: The march to using ES modules has been going on for years, but if you’re still holding out, there’s probably a good reason why? However, while you can maintain packages supporting both ESM and CommonJS, Anthony thinks it’s time to go ‘ESM only’ and explains why.
articles.author: Anthony Fu

articles.title: How and Why to Build 'Copy Code' Buttons
articles.description: A commonly encountered way to give readers easier access to source shared on the Web. David Bushell has an interesting followup reflecting on his own experiences implementing the same feature.
articles.author: Salma Alam-Naylor

articles.title: The RegExp Escaping ECMAScript Proposal
articles.description: RegExp.escape() is a function to create an escaped version of a supplied text that matches itself when used as, or in, a regular expression. Axel has also written an implementation in plain JS to get a feel for how it works.
articles.author: Dr. Axel Rauschmayer

articles.title: How to Start a React Project in 2025
articles.description: While there are many ways to start a React project, Robin examines the pros and cons of a few popular approaches.
articles.author: Robin Wieruch

articles.title: Learning How to Build Modern Web Extensions
articles.description: It’s easy to run into outdated docs when building extensions. Lucky for us, Hui has been through the process and shares some tips.
articles.author: Hui Jing

articles.title: Testing 10 JavaScript Frameworks on Their HTML Defaults
articles.description: Using a JavaScript framework is now ‘the way’ for many Web site developers, but how do the popular options fare at producing valid, error free HTML?
articles.author: Jens Oliver Meiert

articles.title: Ohm: A Parsing Toolkit for JavaScript and TypeScript
articles.description: It’s been a few years since we covered this project and it’s come along a lot. It’s a library for building PEG-based parsers you can use in interpreter, compilers, analysis tools, etc. and you can even play with its grammar online.
articles.author: Warth, Dubroy, et al.

articles.title: Human Regex: Human-Friendly Regular Expression Builder with English Syntax
articles.description: After 8 years of Perl, regexes are my friend, but most developers aren’t big fans? This library offers a natural, fluent approach. Magic Regexp and Super Expressive are alternatives to consider.
articles.author: Ridwan Ajibola

articles.title: Svader: Create GPU-Rendered Svelte Components
articles.description: The examples are a good way to get a feel for what this offers.
articles.author: Holger Dal Mogensen

articles.title: web-worker 1.5: Consistent Web Workers for the Browser and Node
articles.description: Want to publish npm modules that use Web Workers and that work in both Node and client-side? In Node, it works as a web-compatible Worker implementation atop worker_threads. In the browser, it’s an alias for Worker.
articles.author: Jason Miller

articles.title: The React Data Table I Always Wanted
articles.description: A look into a particularly fast and clean shadcn/ui-based data table component (GitHub repo). See a live demo.
articles.author: Maximilian Kaske

articles.title: GitHub Extends Its Monaspace Font Family
articles.description: Monaspace is a fantastic set of monospaced fonts from GitHub targeted at coding use cases. Its new v1.2 release ups the ante by including Nerd Fonts support and symbols, new box drawing glyphs, characters, character variants, ligatures, and more.
articles.author: GitHub

articles.description: 🤔 Developer industry analyst Kate Holterhoff asks "Is npm enough?" and questions why there are so many attempts to replace or extend npm in the JS package registry space.
📱 The React Native team has a roundup of what happened at the most recent contributor summit. Must read for React Native devs.
The Popover API is now considered a 'baseline' browser feature with broad support across all major browsers.

🤖 Reader Ishan Anand has been working on implementing GPT2 (a precursor to OpenAI's current offerings) entirely in the browser to power some interesting browser-based spreadsheet data processing experiments.
Node.js v23.8.0 (Current) and Node.js v22.14.0 (LTS)
Node.js v20.18.3 (LTS) – The backporting of import attributes and JSON modules is now stable.
pnpm 10.3 – The fast, efficiency-focused package manager adds a strict-dep-builds option to exit with a non-zero exit code if any dependencies have unreviewed build scripts.
Pixi.js 8.8 – Fast, flexible 2D WebGL renderer.
Astro 5.3, Prettier 3.5, Electron 34.2

articles.title: Launching Interop 2025
articles.description: This year’s Interop project (an ongoing cross-browser effort to increase interoperability of key web platform features) features 19 focus areas including CSS anchor positioning, Core Web Vitals, the View Transition API, and WebAssembly. You can see the full list, with explanations, in the Interop repo and monitor progress on this dashboard. The WebKit team has shared a blog post going into even more depth and the Microsoft Edge team gives its take too.
articles.author: James Graham

articles.title: Three Approaches to the & Selector in CSS
articles.description: The & selector in vanilla CSS, now supported via CSS Nesting, allows nesting styles within a parent selector without needing preprocessors like Sass. Here’s a look at some of the nuances behind its use.
articles.author: Preethi Sam

articles.title: Learning How to Build Modern Web Extensions
articles.description: It’s easy to run into outdated docs when building extensions. Lucky for us, Hui has been through the process recently and shares some tips.
articles.author: Hui Jing

articles.title: Testing 10 JavaScript Frameworks on Their HTML Defaults
articles.description: Using a JavaScript framework is now ‘the way’ for many Web site developers, but how do the popular options fare at producing valid, error free HTML?
articles.author: Jens Oliver Meiert

articles.title: Decoding CSS Selectors: :has(:not) vs :not(:has)
articles.description: When you combine CSS functions, the nesting matters - a lot.
articles.author: Polypane

articles.title: StyleObserver: A Library to Observe CSS Property Changes
articles.description: An exhaustively tested JS library from Lea Verou, designed to observe any changes to CSS properties, and deftly deflecting a mass of relevant browser bugs along the way. Project homepage.
articles.author: Lea Verou

articles.title: LaLoka Layouts: 30+ Useful Components Built with Tailwind
articles.description: Includes components not normally included in these types of component sets. For example, various fixed position elements, input add-ons, along with standard options like avatars and cards.
articles.author: LaLoka Labs

articles.title: Heat.js: A Heat Map Visualization Library
articles.description: Think like the GitHub contributions heat map. No dependencies, small, responsive, and themeable. There’s a live demo or its GitHub repo.
articles.author: William Troup

articles.title: scroll-snap 5.0: A Customizable Scroll Snap Implementation
articles.description: Uses requestAnimationFrame() for 60fps scrolling performance and doesn’t have any dependencies. Try it here.
articles.author: Luca Falasco

articles.title: tailwind-merge 3.0: Efficiently Merge Tailwind CSS Classes without Conflicts
articles.description: Provides a way to merge Tailwind CSS classes from JavaScript without style conflicts. v3.0 is notably Tailwind CSS v4 only so don’t upgrade if you haven’t upgraded Tailwind CSS first.
articles.author: Dany Castillo

articles.title: dash.js 5.0: JS Implementation of MPEG DASH Playback for Browsers
articles.description: A reference client implementation for the playback of MPEG DASH (Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP) via JavaScript in browser based environments that support the Media Source Extensions. GitHub repo.
articles.author: Dash Industry Forum
